messages:
alex_support: Hey team — Acme reporting intermittent 502s and says their proxy (customer-managed) is stripping our request-id headers. Need a short, copy-paste checklist to send them so we can get a session token + the proxy span for escalation.

priya_se: Quick checklist (short):
• HAR from browser/embedded webview (Chrome Export)
• Single curl that reproduces the call (capture response headers)
• SDK logs showing outgoing request headers + any SDK correlation header
• Console debug token or server-side span/log excerpt

sam_oncall: Add a tiny how-to for each — customers like copy/paste. Also note common proxies (ALB/CloudFront/Cloudflare/NGINX) that may drop headers; ask them to check proxy config for `preserve-host`/`preserve-headers` settings. :warning:

alex_support: Copyable curl to ask customer to run (plain text):
```
# replace $URL and $API_KEY
curl -i -X POST "$URL/v1/generate" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"input":"hello"}' \
  2>&1 | sed -n '1,200p'
```
Ask them to paste the full response header block. We look for `x-rw-request-id`, `x-rw-span-id`, or `x-request-id`.

priya_se: For Node SDK quick snippet (ask them to run locally and paste console output):
```js
const res = await client.generate({input: 'hi'});
console.log('status', res.status);
console.log('headers', res.headers); // look for x-rw-* or x-request-id
```
If using our browser SDK, ask them to open devtools -> Network -> click the request -> Headers -> Response Headers and screenshot or copy.

sam_oncall: HAR export steps (short copy/paste):
1) Open DevTools (F12) -> Network tab
2) Reproduce the failing request
3) Right click -> Save as HAR with content -> attach file
Note: if they use an embedded webview, use remote debugging or have the app generate a HAR via the debug SDK helper (we can share instructions if needed).

alex_support: If they suspect the proxy removed headers, ask them to capture the proxy's raw backend request/response headers (not the client-facing ones). For common infra: ALB/NGINX/CloudFront you can enable access logs or captured header logging for a short window. Example wording to give to their infra team: 
"Please capture the backend request/response headers for the timeframe 2026-03-15T14:20:00Z to 2026-03-15T14:25:00Z for traffic from our client IPs. We're specifically looking for any `x-rw-*` or `x-request-id` headers and whether they are present when the request reaches our edge."

priya_se: If they cannot share headers due to PII/compliance, request a debug token from the Console (Console -> Support -> Create Debug Token) and the approximate timestamp + client IP. With a debug token we can fetch traces from the private control plane (for Dedicated/Private) and correlate.

alex_support: Minimal information we need to open an eng escalation: 
• One curl output (with -i) showing response headers OR HAR
• SDK log snippet that shows outgoing headers
• Debug token OR proxy raw header excerpt (one of these is enough)
• Approx timestamp (UTC) and tenant/org id if on Dedicated/Private

sam_oncall: Quick troubleshooting hints to include in the note to customer: 
• Try curl directly to our edge (bypass proxy) — if request-id shows up, proxy is the culprit.
• If using TLS termination at the proxy, ensure headers aren't rewritten/removed (look for `proxy_set_header` in nginx).

ingest-bot: Reminder: when they attach a debug token, include the thread URL and the tenant id in the escalation ticket so runtime team can scope the logs.

alex_support: I'll paste this into the customer reply. If they come back with partial data (e.g., only a HAR or only a timestamp), post here and we'll determine next step. :thumbsup:
